Measuring buttermilk

A cup of buttermilk weighs about 245 g, a hair more than whole milk. Store-bought buttermilk is cultured low-fat milk, thicker than milk but still pourable, so measure it in a liquid cup.

If you don't have any, the usual fix is 1 tablespoon of lemon juice or white vinegar in a liquid cup, topped up to the 1 cup line with milk. Let it sit for five to ten minutes until it thickens slightly. It weighs close enough to real buttermilk that you can swap it gram for gram.

Buttermilk's acid is what reacts with baking soda in pancakes, biscuits and soda bread. If you swap in plain milk instead, the recipe usually needs baking powder in place of some of the soda.

Source: USDA FoodData Central (245 g per cup, cultured buttermilk); King Arthur Baking lists 227 g.

Questions

How many grams is ½ cup of buttermilk?

½ cup of buttermilk weighs about 123 g (4.32 oz). A full cup is 245 g.

How many cups is 100 grams of buttermilk?

100 g of buttermilk is about ⅜ cup, based on 245 g per cup.

Can I use milk with lemon juice instead of buttermilk?

Yes. Put 1 tablespoon of lemon juice or vinegar in a cup, add milk to the 1 cup line and let it stand 5 to 10 minutes. Use it in the same amount, by volume or weight.
